sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the distinction between the capacity for Sefiros in Ein Sof and the connection of Ein Sof to Sefiros, clarifying that the former is a result of the latter through the elevation of mayin nukvin.

translations.translation: Now, it was explained above
(sections 4-5)
in the interpretation of the verse "as water reflects the face back to the face,"
that just as in water in its simple sense,
by looking into them,
the image of the face that looks into them is seen in them,
so too is it in the supernal waters,
the simplicity of Ein Sof,
that through the elevation of mayin nukvin of the Sefiros
(faces)
to Ein Sof,
the matter of the Sefiros is made in Him—the concealed Sefiros.
And that through the elevation of mayin nukvin, Sefiros are made in Ein Sof, is because even beforehand He has a connection to Sefiros
[analogous to water,
that the image of the face that looks into them is seen in them because the water and the face are of the same type of existence],
and explanation is needed,
for since even the concealed Sefiros
(the faces seen in the water)
are only the capacity for Sefiros
(as above, section 7),
and on the other hand,
also the Ein Sof that is above the concealed Sefiros
(the water in which the faces are seen)
has a connection to Sefiros,
what is the difference between these two matters?
And the explanation of this can be said,
that the matter of capacity for something is—that the thing can be.
For although capacity is not the source of the thing, and its matter is that the essence is able
[as known the distinction between koach and yecholes56],
nevertheless,
that the essence is able,
is—that it is within the capacity of the essence that it be thus and so.
And the connection of Ein Sof to Sefiros
(water to face)
is
(not that from the aspect of Ein Sof Sefiros can be,
but rather the opposite)
that the form of Sefiros can be in Ein Sof.
And although even this matter is a descent relative to Ein Sof as He is in His own essence,
for in Ein Sof as He is in His own essence there is no relation at all to the matter of Sefiros
[and as above, section 5, that it is analogous to intellectual logic that has no connection at all to colors,
whiteness and redness],
but after it arose in His will that there be a place of reception for the elevation of mayin nukvin of the Sefiros, through this a connection to the Sefiros was made for Him
(as above),
nevertheless,
the place of reception of the elevation of mayin nukvin of the Sefiros is that their mayin nukvin will take hold of a place with Him,
that through the elevation there will be a drawing down of Ein Sof,
and therefore,
the connection of Ein Sof to Sefiros that is made through the elevation of mayin nukvin of the Sefiros taking hold of a place with Him,
is that in Ein Sof it is possible for the form of Sefiros to be.
And therefore,
the capacity for Sefiros,
since its matter is that Sefiros can be,
is called by the name Sefiros,
the ten concealed Sefiros,
and the term "atzilus" is said regarding it
[and as brought above, section 7, from the discourses "He emanated ten names"],
and moreover,
that this capacity for Sefiros is made in Ein Sof is not from the aspect of Ein Sof, but rather through the elevation of mayin nukvin of the Sefiros.
And the descent, so to speak, in Ein Sof that He be in a manner that through the elevation of mayin nukvin the faces of the Sefiros are seen in Him,
is not that some matter is emanated in Him,
but rather it is Ein Sof Himself,
analogous to water that is in such a manner that the face that looks into it is seen in it.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the faces seen in the water are not a separate entity from the water but the water itself, and likewise the concealed Sefiros are not separate from Ein Sof but are Ein Sof Himself, having both an external aspect of capacity and an internal aspect of Ein Sof.

translations.translation: Now, it is explained in the discourses57,
that the faces seen in the water,
since they are from the aspect of the faces that look, and not from the aspect of the water,
therefore they are not a thing separate from the water, but rather the water itself.
For if the seen faces were drawn from the water,
then they would be a separate thing generated from the water
(analogous to fish in the sea).
But since the seen faces are not from the aspect of the water,
they are not a separate thing generated from the water, but rather the water itself.
— And so too is it in the analogue,
that since that in Ein Sof there are the ten concealed Sefiros is through the elevation of mayin nukvin of the Sefiros
(and not that they were generated from Ein Sof),
therefore they are not a thing separate from Ein Sof, but rather they are Ein Sof Himself.
And based on this,
in the concealed Sefiros there are two matters.
In their externality,
their matter is—capacity for Sefiros,
and in their inwardness,
they are—Ein Sof.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that through the service of the lower man, the inwardness of the upper man is revealed, which is the simplicity of Ein Sof, enabling the form of the lower man to be in the upper man, as water reflects face to face.

translations.translation: Now, it was explained above in section 4, that in "water reflects the face back to the face,"
there are two matters.
That the image of the face that looks into the water is seen in the water,
and that this image is afterwards seen by the man who looks into them.
That is,
that the image seen by the man is the image seen in the water.
And so too is it in the analogue,
that through the elevation of mayin nukvin of the lower faces,
the Sefiros of Atzilus,
faces are made
(the concealed Sefiros)
in the water
(the simplicity of Ein Sof),
and afterwards the upper faces that are in the water are drawn and revealed
(the concealed Sefiros)
from above to below, and from this the lower faces are made,
the Sefiros of Atzilus.
That is, that the matter of the revealed Sefiros
(in their inwardness)
is—the revelation of the concealed Sefiros,
analogous to the image of the face seen by the man who looks into the water, which is the image seen in the water
(the concealed Sefiros).
And based on the above, that the image seen in the water is the water itself,
it is understood,
that also the lower faces
(the Sefiros of Atzilus),
which are the revelation of the upper faces,
their inner matter is—water,
the simplicity of Ein Sof.
And based on this, what is said "as water reflects the face back to the face, so is the heart of man to man" will be understood,
that just as in water
(the simplicity of Ein Sof),
through the elevation of mayin nukvin, faces are made in them
(Sefiros),
so too is it in the upper man,
that through the elevation of mayin nukvin of the lower man, the form and image of the lower man is made in the upper man.
For at first glance,
the reason that the image of the face that looks into them is seen in water is because water is simple,
but not so when one looks into something that has a form,
the form of that thing contradicts the shape of the face that looks into it
(as above, section 5),
and since the upper man
(the Sefiros of Atzilus)
is a level of form,
how can it be that the form of the lower man be in him?
And the explanation of this,
that through the service of the lower man, the inwardness of the upper man is revealed,
the Sefiros of Atzilus,
whose matter is—the revelation of the concealed Sefiros
(faces seen in the water),
to the extent that they are the water
(the simplicity of Ein Sof)
itself.
And through the revelation
(through the service of the lower man)
of the inwardness of the upper man,
which is the simplicity of Ein Sof,
it is possible for the form of the lower man to be in Him58.
And based on this, it can be said that "as water reflects the face back to the face" is also the reason and explanation for "so is the heart of man to man."
For the matter of "water reflects the face back to the face" is that the lower faces seen outside the water
(the revealed Sefiros)
are one with the upper faces seen in the water
(the concealed Sefiros)
to the extent that they are one with the water itself
(the simplicity of Ein Sof),
and this is the reason for "the heart of man to man,"
that in the upper man the form of the lower man is made.
